transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: Tue Oct 05 2027 09:00 PT / Recorded at: 2027-10-05T16:00:00Z / Duration: 52 min
Attendees: Alex Morgan (Redwood CSM), Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Raman (Redwood SE), Sam Ortiz (Redwood Onboarding), Emily Park (Verdant Head of Data), Marcus Hayes (Verdant CTO), Laura Chen (Verdant Security), Ben Torres (Verdant IT Ops), Aisha Malik (Verdant Product)

Summary:
- Kickoff for Verdant Clinic onboarding to Redwood Inference.
- Covered project timeline, roles, security/compliance needs, pilot scope, and technical deep-dive next steps.
- Agreement to provision test tenant and schedule SE deep dive next week; customer will share sample prompts and traffic profile.

Topics:
- Pilot goals and success criteria
- SSO/SSAML and SSO setup, audit logs, KMS
- Deployment mode: hosted vs dedicated vs private/VPC
- Performance targets (latency/cost tradeoffs) and benchmark plan
- Onboarding timeline and responsibilities

Transcript:
[00:00] Alex Morgan: hey everyone thanks for joining, we can wait a minute for folks to hop on but want to cover kickoff items and make sure roles are clear
[00:24] Jordan Lee: hi all Jordan from Redwood, I'll be the AE on this account, here to help unblock procurement and pricing stuff
[00:35] Emily Park: thanks Jordan, Emily here; excited to get going, we've got a few big security questions so Laura will cover those
[00:49] Laura Chen: hi yes i'll flag the compliance bits, SOC two, encryption at rest, k m s, and audit log retention are the big ones
[01:05] Priya Raman: hey team Priya (SE) - i'll run the technical deep dive, we'll look at latency, batching, kv cache behavior and model selection for your workloads
[01:22] Marcus Hayes: hi Marcus here, we want sub-300ms p95 for our chat use-case ideally, and need guidance on cost at scale
[01:36] Priya Raman: ok noted, we'll show options - hosted with caching and batching, dedicated GPU pool, and an on-prem / private control-plane path if you need VPC isolation
[01:52] Ben Torres: quick Q - for private deployments, do you support our HSM and KMS keys? we use AWS KMS and have an HSM for some secrets
[02:07] Alex Morgan: yes we integrate with customer KMS providers and support bring-your-own-key; we'll share the KMS integration doc, but exact HSM certs we can cover in security review
[02:26] Jordan Lee: for pricing FYI there's usage-based for hosted and reserved capacity for dedicated; Sam will coordinate test tenant provisioning
[02:40] Sam Ortiz: I can provision a sandbox tenant today, but I'll need a contact and a list of allowed IP ranges and SAML issuer metadata
[02:56] Emily Park: i'll get that to you, we also want to run a 6-week pilot with a small subset of traffic to validate latency and quality
[03:12] Priya Raman: great, for pilot we'll do a baseline benchmark (synthetic) and a few real traffic passes; we'll measure token costs, p95 latency, and correctness on your prompt set
[03:32] Laura Chen: on auditability, we need per-request logs stored 12 months, and ability to redact PHI when required. how's that handled?
[03:49] Alex Morgan: we have configurable log retention and the ability to disable full transcript retention for sensitive flows; we'll share the data handling and redaction playbook
[04:05] Marcus Hayes: is there automatic fallback if the model is overloaded or region is down? concern about outages during peak hours
[04:20] Priya Raman: yes we support smart routing, fallback to compatible model variants, and multi-region routing for HA; we'll demo routing policies in the technical deep dive
[04:36] Jordan Lee: also want to flag enterprise agreements - Laura and Marcus, we'll share the security pack and standard addenda; procurement items can be fasttracked once pilot shows results
[04:54] Emily Park: timeline question - what's realistic for SSO + tenant provisioning and starting the pilot?
[05:07] Sam Ortiz: SSO setup + tenant provisioning can be done in 2-3 business days after we get metadata and IP allowlist; pilot start depends on when you can share sample prompts/data
[05:25] Emily Park: we can share sample prompts and a redacted dataset by friday (2027-10-08)
[05:37] Priya Raman: perfect. For the actual model: do you have a preference for open models or Redwood-managed models? open models sometimes cost less but can vary in quality
[05:52] Marcus Hayes: open is fine if quality is stable; we need a consistent SLA though if we move to production. Also curious about quantization options to reduce cost
[06:08] Priya Raman: we'll present quantized model profiles and expected latency/cost tradeoffs. For SLA-backed production, Dedicated is the route - reserved GPU pools and predictable throughput
[06:24] Laura Chen: encryption at rest, key rotation policies and audit logs - can you share the whitepaper?
[06:36] Alex Morgan: yes will share SOC2, ISO, KMS integration notes and a whitepaper on encryption and key rotation
[06:50] Jordan Lee: on measurement - let's agree pilot success criteria now: 1) p95 latency under 300ms for chat under pilot load, 2) token cost within target range we define, 3) no major quality regressions on 100 eval prompts
[07:10] Emily Park: that seems fair. We'll add a fourth: compliance checklist satisfied for pilot scope (audit logs + redaction rules)
[07:25] Priya Raman: noted. We'll also include a benchmark spreadsheet - we'll populate baseline numbers and then run two test passes during pilot
[07:38] Ben Torres: network question - for hosted mode, do you need outbound firewall rules? we prefer only egress to specific endpoints
[07:50] Sam Ortiz: yes, we can provide a list of endpoints and IP ranges; we also support VPC peering for private deployments if you prefer no public egress
[08:04] Laura Chen: for data residency: some data must stay in us-east-1, is region pinning supported?
[08:16] Priya Raman: yes region pinning is supported, we can route requests to specific regions and keep logs in region as well, we'll document retention rules per region
[08:30] Marcus Hayes: curious about observability - can we get per-route token cost and latency breakdowns in console?
[08:42] Alex Morgan: Redwood Console gives per-route and per-model dashboards, token-level cost, traces and error analysis; we'll grant you access to a demo console in the sandbox tenant
[08:58] Emily Park: good, that will help product measure cost vs latency tradeoffs
[09:12] Jordan Lee: procurement note - if we need enterprise agreements, we'll loop legal, but pilot can proceed under standard terms then convert to enterprise contract after pilot success
[09:28] Marcus Hayes: for the technical deep dive next week can we include our latency-sensitive workflows and a hands-on run of the benchmark?
[09:42] Priya Raman: absolutely, we'll run a live benchmark, show KV cache effects, batching settings, and model quantization impact. please share peak qps and average seq len beforehand
[09:58] Emily Park: avg tokens per request is around 120, peak qps about 25 in our test window, but post-PT rollout could spike higher
[10:12] Priya Raman: ok that'll inform kernel selection and batching config; we'll include suggestions for continuous batching and prefix caching to reduce per-token cost
[10:26] Laura Chen: one more on governance - do you support role-based access control and audit logs for who invoked what?
[10:39] Alex Morgan: yes RBAC is supported via SSO and console roles; audit logs map to user-level actions and we can surface them to your SIEM via syslog or export
[10:54] Ben Torres: can we sandbox with our own model weights later if we want to bring a private model?
[11:06] Priya Raman: we support bringing custom model variants into Private deployments; there are cert and packaging requirements, we'll cover that in an integration doc
[11:21] Jordan Lee: ok let's recap next steps and owners
[11:28] Alex Morgan: recap: Redwood to send onboarding deck, security pack, KMS integration docs; Sam to provision sandbox and API keys; Priya to run technical deep dive and benchmarks; Verdant to share samples, SAML metadata, and traffic profile.
[11:49] Emily Park: sounds good. target to start pilot week of 2027-10-11?
[11:55] Priya Raman: that should work as long as we get metadata and samples this week
[12:05] Marcus Hayes: agreed; we'll prioritize and get the package to Sam by Friday
[12:13] Alex Morgan: great thanks everyone, we'll follow up with meeting notes and calendar invites for the deep-dive
[12:20] Meeting end
